content.thinking: I need to adjust two phrasings: changing "logged {G5309.1} times between {G5309.3}" to "logged {G5309.1} times over {G5309.3}", and "from {Gce95.4} every evaluation" to "over {Gce95.4} every evaluation logged was on".

action_items.item: Roll out feature flag changes on io-shop to a small share of traffic first, and widen them only after the account page error rate is checked.
Automatically switch a feature flag on io-shop back off when the error rate alert fires soon after that flag was switched on.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of requests that failed rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and reached {errors_at_worst} at worst. The service's own warning about the account page error rate peaked at {Gbac1.5} at {Gbac1.7}.

Account page requests were failing with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, logged {G5309.1} times over {G5309.3}. Before the onset the only failures logged were shoppers closing the connection, and account pages rendered normally.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: the search for production changes in the day before the onset came back with the flag change alone, and no deploys.
A rollout still in progress: at {T10.1} all {T10.2} replicas ran one revision.
Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before {T15.4}, matching P1.

causal_chain.step: Account page renders had begun going through the monthly spend summary path, because an admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. In the minute of {G971b.6}, flag evaluations split off {G971b.1} / on {G971b.2}, and over {Gce95.4} every evaluation logged was on. Before that the flag was logged off. In Code-Fix's reading, render_spend_summary only calls the failing function when use_monthly_summary is true.

The newly enabled path fails for some shoppers. average_spend_per_item_this_month divides the shopper's total for this month by the number of purchases marked as in the current month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the line raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1}, the line the logged error points to.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a feature setting made the account page run a calculation that likely divides by the number of items a shopper bought this month, and that fails for shoppers who have bought before but nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen covering the monthly spend summary for a shopper with past purchases but none this month before monthly-spend-feature was switched on. Code-Fix says the two cases it adds are written to raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The empty case would have failed in a test before the flag was switched on, and account pages would not have failed in production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag change reached most traffic within its first minute and all traffic soon after. No staged rollout or error-rate check on the flag change was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have hit the failing path before the rise in errors showed, and the flag could have been held back before it reached everyone.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature back off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed {T21.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised that the service was no longer at the incident's level.
The Investigator placed the onset at {T6.2}, the same minute the flag was switched on, which tied the failures to that change.
Code-Fix proposed a fix as draft pull request PR #366, with two new tests.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, render_spend_summary calls average_spend_per_item_this_month. That function divides the shopper's total for this month by the number of purchases marked as this month's. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py and the account page request fails, because nothing in the files Code-Fix read handles the empty case.
input.still_at_risk: The division is still in the code, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers who have bought before but nothing this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
